jobs.description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title and Summary

Manager, Business Strategy COVEC

Manager Business Strategy COVEC

Overview

Reporting directly to the Vice President, Business Strategy, South LAC, with a dual reporting line to the COVEC Cluster Lead, this role leads Mastercard’s strategy agenda across Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Guyana, and Suriname, while supporting broader South Division priorities.

As a member of both the South LAC Strategy team and the COVEC Leadership Team, the role partners across the organization to shape strategic priorities, identify new growth opportunities, evaluate investments and business initiatives, support key decision-making processes, and drive execution against critical business objectives. The position works closely with leadership teams across markets, products, services, operations, finance, legal, public affairs, people, and other functions to ensure alignment, mobilize resources, and deliver measurable business impact.

The role serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, helping translate market opportunities, industry trends, and business challenges into actionable strategies that accelerate growth, strengthen Mastercard’s competitive position, and support the delivery of cluster and divisional objectives.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead the development and execution of Mastercard’s strategic priorities across COVEC and support selected South Division initiatives.
• Identify, assess, and prioritize growth opportunities across customers, products, services, payment flows, partnerships, and emerging business models.
• Develop market assessments, business cases, financial analyses, strategic recommendations, and investment evaluations to support decision-making and resource allocation.
• Drive strategic initiatives from concept through execution, coordinating across multiple stakeholders and ensuring alignment with business objectives.
• Support annual strategic planning, business reviews, operating reviews, and executive governance processes.
• Monitor performance against strategic objectives and key business metrics, identifying risks, opportunities, and actions required to drive results.
• Develop presentations, reports, and recommendations for regional, divisional, and global leadership audiences.
• Provide insights on industry trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and emerging opportunities impacting Mastercard and its customers.
• Support special projects, executive requests, and other high-priority initiatives across the cluster and division.

All About You

• 8+ years of experience in strategy, management consulting, business development, financial services, payments, fintech, or related industries.
• Demonstrated ability to lead complex strategic and cross-functional initiatives in dynamic environments.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including business case development, market assessment, financial analysis, and strategic planning.
• Ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights and actionable recommendations.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment across a matrixed organization.
• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including experience preparing materials for executive audiences.
• Self-starter with strong project management skills and a proven ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
• Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
• Fluent in English and Spanish.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
- Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

- Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

- Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

- Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.description:
Our Purpose

We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Title and Summary

Manager, Smart Acquirer Services (SAS) Commercial Program Management

Manager, Smart Acquirer Services (SAS) Program Management
About Mastercard
Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments sector. We power payments and provide products and services for individuals and industries around the world. Our people, technology, data and brand provide the capabilities that drive our success. We believe in connecting people to priceless possibilities.

Overview
Mastercard’s Global Acceptance & Merchant Solutions team is transforming the acquiring ecosystem through Smart Acquirer Services (SAS), a strategic initiative designed to deliver a single access point to Mastercard acceptance, security, performance optimization and innovation capabilities through Merchant Cloud. SAS is being commercialized globally across multiple regions and markets, requiring a scalable operating model, governance framework, commercialization playbooks and market rollout strategy.''

The Manager, Smart Acquirer Services Program Management will serve as the central program lead responsible for driving end-to-end execution of the SAS initiative globally. This individual will act as the connective tissue across Product, Finance, Legal, Regional Teams, Controllers, Services, Implementation, Customer Delivery and Commercialization teams to ensure successful launch and scale of SAS across priority markets.
This role requires a highly organized commercial PMO leader capable of managing complex global initiatives, driving accountability across workstreams, building scalable playbooks and ensuring market readiness from business case through launch and adoption.

Role

As Manager, SAS Program Management, you will be responsible for establishing and operating the global program office supporting Smart Acquirer Services.
You will own the planning, governance, execution and reporting framework required to successfully launch and scale SAS across multiple markets and regions.
• Global Program Leadership: Establish and manage the overall SAS program governance model, including executive steering committees, working groups, weekly program reviews, milestones, dependencies, risk registers and escalation paths.
• Country Commercialization Playbooks: Build and maintain a repeatable SAS commercialization framework that can be deployed market by market, starting with priority markets including South Africa, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Georgia and Mauritius.
• Market Qualification & Readiness: Coordinate revenue opportunity assessments, business case development and readiness reviews across commercial opportunity, competitive landscape, regulatory considerations, sponsorship, stakeholder alignment and launch qualification criteria.
• Product & Bundle Governance: Coordinate global decisions regarding SAS bundle composition, product inclusion and exclusion governance, regional product requirements, rollout sequencing and alignment with the product roadmap.
• Business Cases, Pricing & Finance: Partner with Finance, Controllers and Pricing teams to establish market business cases, revenue allocation methodologies, RPIC approvals and tracking of projected and realized revenue impact by market.
• Commercialization & Go-to-Market Execution: Coordinate regional commercialization workstreams, develop market-level rollout plans, drive acquirer prioritization, customer engagement planning, roadshows, enablement programs and launch readiness activities.
• Implementation & Customer Delivery: Partner with implementation and delivery teams to establish standardized onboarding processes for acquirer onboarding, Merchant Cloud provisioning, certification, customer acceptance testing and go-live readiness reviews.
• Launch Governance & Adoption: Manage launch approval processes and decision gates, define adoption KPIs and success metrics, build executive dashboards and track adoption, activation and revenue realization across markets.
Success Metrics
• Number of markets launched on schedule.
• Revenue impact delivered versus business case.
• Country readiness and approval cycle times.
• Acquirer onboarding and adoption rates.
• Commercialization milestone attainment.
• Program governance effectiveness.
• Executive stakeholder satisfaction.
• Program risk mitigation and issue resolution.
All About You
• Proven experience leading complex global programs, PMOs or strategic transformations.
• Strong background in payments, acquiring, acceptance, gateways or value-added services.

Mastercard Transaction Services (MTS) enables secure, innovative and regulated money movement services globally. As the business grows and evolves, we are seeking an experienced Director, Technology Risk Management to strengthen independent technology risk oversight across our regulated entities and help advance the wider MTS Risk Management Framework.

This is a highly visible leadership role within the second line of defence. Technology risk is the primary focus, spanning technology, cyber, operational resilience, outsourcing and third-party risk. The successful candidate will also contribute across broader risk disciplines, including risk appetite, risk assessments, issue and risk event management, governance, reporting, policy and framework development.

Working with senior leaders across Technology, Engineering, Product, Cyber Security, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs and Legal Entity Management, you will provide credible challenge, translate complex risk matters into clear business insight, and support sound decision-making within a fast-moving global payments environment.

WHAT WILL YOU BE ACCOUNTABLE FOR
Strategic technology risk oversight
-Lead independent second line oversight and challenge of technology, cyber and operational resilience risks across MTS regulated entities.
-Evaluate material technology initiatives, transformation programmes and strategic investments from a risk perspective.
-Provide credible, evidence-based challenge of technology risk assessments, control environments, risk acceptances, control weaknesses and remediation plans.
-Monitor emerging technology and cyber risks, assess their relevance to MTS, and advise senior stakeholders on potential business and regulatory impacts.
-Oversee second line challenge of outsourcing, critical third-party arrangements, technology dependencies and concentration risks.

Broader Risk Management Framework leadership
-Play a leading role in the continued development, implementation and embedding of the MTS Risk Management Framework beyond the technology risk domain.
-Drive enhancements to risk governance, risk appetite, risk assessment, issue management, risk event management, risk acceptance and reporting processes.
-Contribute to the development and maintenance of risk policies, standards, methodologies, procedures and guidance.
-Lead or facilitate enterprise and legal entity risk assessments and support consistent application of the framework across regulated entities.
-Provide oversight and challenge of material non-technology risks, issues, events and remediation activities where required by the broader Risk team agenda.
-Partner with first line stakeholders to improve risk identification, assessment, escalation and management practices while preserving second line independence.

Governance, regulatory and Board engagement
-Prepare and present clear risk insights to executive leadership, governance committees and Boards.
-Lead or support regulatory examinations, supervisory engagements, independent reviews, audits and associated remediation programmes.
-Provide subject matter expertise on regulatory expectations relating to technology, operational resilience and broader risk governance.
-Contribute to strategic risk reporting, risk appetite oversight and escalation of material risk matters.

Leadership and influence
-Build trusted relationships across Technology, Engineering, Product and control functions and influence decisions through clear, practical risk advice.
-Promote a strong risk culture and constructive challenge across MTS.
-Mentor and develop risk professionals and contribute to capability building across the wider Risk Management function.
-Operate effectively across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions and risk domains in a complex global organisation.

WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR
Essential experience
-Significant experience in technology risk, cyber risk, operational risk, information security governance, technology controls, IT audit or a related discipline.
-Experience operating at senior level within financial services, payments, banking, fintech or another highly regulated sector.
-Demonstrated ability to provide independent oversight and credible challenge across complex technology environments and change programmes.
-Experience engaging senior executives, governance committees, Boards, regulators, auditors or independent reviewers.
-Proven ability to assess complex risks, identify material themes and translate them into clear, pragmatic recommendations.
-Strong executive communication, stakeholder management and influencing skills.

Desirable experience and knowledge
-Experience designing, implementing, enhancing or embedding an enterprise or legal entity Risk Management Framework.
-Practical experience across broader risk disciplines such as risk appetite, enterprise risk assessments, issue management, risk event management, risk acceptance, policy development and governance reporting.
-Experience working across technology and non-technology risk domains rather than within a single specialist discipline.
-Knowledge of payment systems, money movement platforms, e-money institutions or regulated payment service providers.
-Experience supporting regulatory examinations, supervisory engagements, remediation programmes or regulatory change initiatives.
-Knowledge of operational resilience, business continuity, outsourcing and third-party risk management.
-Experience working across multiple regulated entities or jurisdictions.

Qualifications
-A bachelor's degree in technology, information security, computer science, risk management or a related discipline is preferred. Relevant professional experience will also be considered.
-Professional certifications such as CRISC, CISSP, CISM, CISA, COBIT or ITIL are desirable.

The leadership profile
-Credible technology risk leader with the breadth to contribute to the full Risk Management Framework.
-Independent and appropriately challenging, with a collaborative and solutions-oriented style.
-Comfortable moving between strategic governance, regulatory priorities and detailed risk matters.
-Able to create clarity from complexity and focus stakeholders on material risks and outcomes.
-Committed to high standards of integrity, judgement and second line independence.

WHY JOIN MASTERCARD
-Influence technology risk management across a global, regulated money movement business.
-Help shape the evolution of the broader MTS Risk Management Framework.
-Engage directly with senior leaders, governance forums and regulatory stakeholders.
-Work on complex challenges spanning technology, cyber security, operational resilience, governance and enterprise risk.
-Make a meaningful contribution to the safety, resilience and responsible growth of Mastercard Transaction Services.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
- Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

- Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

- Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

- Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

Mastercard’s Customer Risk Management (CRM) team plays a critical role in safeguarding the integrity and resilience of the global payments ecosystem. CRM, which manages Mastercard’s credit and counterparty risk management activities, is responsible for managing approximately USD 75 billion in customer credit exposure globally, ensuring risks are identified, assessed, monitored, and mitigated in support of Mastercard’s continued growth and innovation.
We are seeking a Manager, Customer Credit Risk Management to join our Asia Pacific team based in Gurgaon. This role focuses on assessing and managing credit and counterparty risk across a diverse portfolio of participants within Mastercard’s network, including banks, non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), fintechs, payment companies, issuers, acquirers, and other players in the payment ecosystem. The role will be responsible for identifying, assessing, and monitoring credit risk for assigned markets in accordance with Mastercard’s policies and procedures, including the CRM Procedures of the Credit Risk Policy.
The role offers significant exposure to senior stakeholders across Risk, Finance, Franchise, Product, and business development functions, as well as opportunities to influence key business decisions and strategic initiatives across Asia Pacific.
This is an exciting opportunity for professionals with experience in credit risk management and who are looking to expand their expertise within the rapidly evolving global payments industry.

________________________________________
Role Responsibilities:
The primary responsibility of this role is to ensure that customer and counterparty risks within assigned markets are appropriately identified, assessed, monitored, and mitigated in accordance with Mastercard’s risk appetite, policies, and procedures.
This role requires strong technical knowledge of credit analysis/underwriting, along with familiarity with Mastercard’s business model. Knowledge and experience in the payments industry will be an added advantage.
Key responsibilities include:
• Conduct comprehensive credit assessments and ongoing monitoring of financial institutions, NBFIs, fintechs, payment companies, and other counterparties across Asia Pacific.
• Analyze financial statements, regulatory filings, capital adequacy, liquidity, profitability, cash flow, and business risk factors to evaluate creditworthiness.
• Recommend internal risk ratings, exposure limits, and risk mitigation strategies in line with Mastercard’s risk management framework.
• Monitor portfolio-level and counterparty-specific risk exposures, identifying emerging risks and recommending appropriate actions.
• Serve as the primary point of contact for customer-specific credit and counterparty risk matters within assigned markets.
• Partner closely with Account Management, Franchise, Product, Finance, and Legal teams to support customer growth initiatives while maintaining prudent risk controls.
• Support customer onboarding activities by ensuring Customer Risk Management requirements are met and customer activations are completed efficiently.
• Develop and implement alternative risk mitigation solutions, including collateral and other credit enhancement structures where appropriate.
• Perform portfolio reviews, trend analysis, and stress assessments to evaluate concentrations, emerging risks, and changing market conditions.
• Support strategic initiatives requiring credit risk analytics, exposure monitoring, portfolio insights, and risk assessments.
• Contribute to the enhancement of risk frameworks, policies, methodologies, monitoring tools, and operational processes.
• Partner with global CRM teams on risk data governance, customer exposure monitoring enhancements, and system testing activities.
• Prepare internal and external risk reporting, including governance materials, audit-related reporting, regulatory submissions, and ad hoc management requests.
• Share best practices and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across the global Customer Risk Management organization.
________________________________________
About You
Required Qualifications:
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related quantitative discipline.
• 4+ years of experience in Credit Risk, Counterparty Risk, Credit Underwriting, Financial Institutions (FIG) Credit, Corporate Banking Credit, Portfolio Management, Treasury Credit Risk, or a related field.
• Strong experience conducting fundamental credit analysis and financial statement analysis.
• Experience assessing banks, non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), fintechs, payment companies, insurance companies, asset managers, or other financial services organizations.
• Demonstrated ability to evaluate credit risks and formulate sound risk recommendations based on quantitative and qualitative analysis.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills with high attention to detail.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present risk assessments and recommendations to stakeholders.

• Support agile methodology compliance, identify barriers to successful delivery, and coordinate resolution or escalation of issues as appropriate.
• Provide input into business processes, standards, plans and service improvements to support effective delivery and sustainable change outcomes.

• in agile change management

• Ability to convert data, delivery information and stakeholder feedback into concise, evidence-based insights, recommendations and actions for different audiences.

- Coordinate with internal stakeholders across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Operations, Product, Finance, and business teams to drive timely completion of regulatory deliverables.

- Experience with regulatory licensing, regulatory reporting, or compliance program management in a financial services, payments, money transmission, fintech, or digital assets environment.
- Strong understanding of regulatory obligations related to money transmission, virtual currency, licensing, examinations, and regulator communications.
- Experience working with NMLS or similar regulatory licensing and filing systems.
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple regulatory deliverables with competing deadlines.

- Ability to work cross-functionally and influence stakeholders without direct authority.

- Experience preparing board or senior management reporting, compliance metrics, and regulatory risk assessment materials.
- Familiarity with regulatory examinations, remediation plans, issue management, and evidence collection.
- Experience coordinating international registrations or reporting obligations, such as FinCEN, FINTRAC, or similar regulatory bodies.
- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment with evolving requirements.

The MTS business unit and the MTS shared services functions are housed under the umbrella of MTS and are comprised of components central to the activities of a licensed payment services firm. These components include:

• Payment/Money transmitter licenses for operating payments business in defined jurisdictions
• Contract definition (associated T&Cs) specific to the MTS entity and its umbrella geographies
• Associated settlement accounts and other services for the relevant MTS entity
• Compliance services including, but not limited to, due diligence, real-time sanctions screening/AML/fraud management, etc.
• Regulatory reporting to the relevant regulators on behalf of the regulated business and its subsequent activities

MTS LAC (MTS Mexico) is the authorized and regulated licensed entity within Mastercard Transaction Services (MTS) in Mexico through which regulated payments activity is undertaken for our Mexico-based customers and others around the world. MTS is a division within Mastercard that undertakes payments business wherever a product or business function requires regulated support.

MTS is seeking an MLRO based in Mexico City who will coordinate and maintain a robust AML/CFT (Countering the Financing of Terrorism) and Sanctions program in alignment with Mexican AML/CFT regulations, including the LFPIORPI, CNBV guidelines, and UIF reporting obligations; internal standards; and regional sanctions reporting obligations.

Additionally, the candidate will drive our customer experience strategy forward by consistently innovating and problem-solving in the Compliance arena. The ideal candidate is passionate about the customer experience journey, highly motivated, intellectually curious, analytical, and possesses an entrepreneurial mindset. The successful candidate will also demonstrate strong communication skills, accountability, sound judgment, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and evolving environment

Role Summary:
The MLRO, MTS Mexico must be knowledgeable and skilled in the relevant AML/CFT/Sanctions Compliance areas. The MLRO will assist the MLRO for North Americas to develop management information systems for regular reporting, including to the MTS US and Mexico Board and Management Committee on the status of the Compliance program and its organization. MTS serves customers based in Mexico and several other countries around the world.

This role requires working as part of a geographically diverse team and a matrix structure collaborating with multiple stakeholders across MTS and the wider Mastercard organization. This role demands excellent, clear, and articulate communication skills, both verbal and written, and the ability to clearly and concisely communicate issues, regulations, and processes.

The role will also support KYC, customer onboarding, due diligence, and regulatory engagement activities across the broader MTS business.

Key Responsibilities:
1. Report and work closely with the Vice President, MLRO for North Americas to determine the effectiveness and efficiency of the Compliance Program and its ability to identify, detect, deter, and report suspicious activity.
2. Ensure timely and accurate submission of reports to the Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF) and other relevant authorities, including STRs, threshold reports, and periodic compliance updates.
3. Serve as the primary liaison with the CNBV and other regulatory bodies, representing MTS Mexico in all AML/CFT-related matters.
4. Review laws and regulations that impact the MTS compliance requirements, with emphasis on the MX AML and Sanctions requirements.
5. Undertake comprehensive risk assessments to determine AML/CFT/Sanctions and other risk exposures through collaboration with other functions to develop mitigating controls as required.
6. Maintain compliance policies, programs, and procedures.
7. Ensure all staff, up to and including the Board, are adequately trained in AML/CFT/Sanctions and other relevant regulations.
8. Disseminate information, answer questions, and serve as a subject matter expert for MTS on Mexico-related Compliance issues.
9. Lead MTS Mexico regulatory examinations and audits, including gathering requested information and developing and coordinating responses to such reviews as necessary.
10. Support the business in an advisory capacity, manage customer due diligence escalations, and where necessary, enhanced due diligence of customer relationships to determine risk and mitigating controls, including KYC and customer onboarding activities.
11. Review regulatory findings against other financial institutions for lessons learned, share with the Board, and complete gap analysis against the MTS Compliance program as necessary.
12. Contribute, as a key member of the Compliance leadership team, to the development and implementation of the wider compliance strategy, including staffing.
13. Manage and oversee the expansion of products and services into Mexico and ensure MTS is meeting the business and regulatory requirements.
14. Monitor regulations and guidance released by Mexican AML/Sanctions authorities.
15. Collaborate with Legal, Regulatory, Compliance, and Product/Shared Services, as well as the wider business, on strategic cross-functional implementation, process improvement, and control enhancement activities.

• Experience with Know Your Customer, customer onboarding, correspondent banking or onboarding financial institutions is highly desirable.
• Experience interacting with regulators and supporting examinations, audits or supervisory reviews is strongly preferred.

The Security Event Management group is seeking a highly motivated and experienced security analyst specializing in Insider Threat.
As an Insider Threat Analyst, you will work within a broader security operations function, responding to cybersecurity events, identifying high-impact insider threats, and undertaking internal investigations.

You will monitor, research, assess, and analyze data and alerts from a suite of security tools, including DLP, EDR, SIEM, and user behavior analytics. You will follow defined investigative paths to ensure consistent resolution of often highly sensitive matters, and prepare and present analysis, findings, and recommendations through briefings and reports to security leads and other stakeholders, including senior legal, privacy, and executive stakeholders.

• Contribute to the Insider Threat Working Group.

• Experience with Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Defender / IRM, Microsoft Sentinel, and Endpoint DLP.

• Relevant industry certifications, such as CISSP, GCIH, GCIA, Security+, or equivalent, are desirable.

passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions,

individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences
enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation,
and delivers better business results.
Technology at Mastercard
What we create today will define tomorrow. Revolutionary technologies that
reshape the digital economy to be more connected and inclusive than ever before.
Safer, faster, more sustainable.
And we need the best people to do it. Technologists who are energized by the
challenges of a truly global network. With the talent and vision to create the critical
systems and products that power global commerce and connect people
everywhere to the vital goods and services they need every day.
Working at Mastercard means being part of a unique culture. Inclusive and diverse,
a rich collaboration of ideas and perspectives. A place that celebrates your
strengths, values your experiences, and offers you the flexibility to shape a career
across disciplines and continents. And the opportunity to work alongside experts
and leaders at every level of the business, improving what exists, and inventing
what’s next.
About the Role
The Business Operations (Biz Ops) team is seeking a Business Operations Site
Reliability Engineer (SRE).
The role of Business Operations Organization is to be the production readiness
steward for Mastercard products. As a Business Operations SRE, we are
responsible for ensuring that our platform is stable and healthy. We break down
barriers to run our products by fostering developer run ownership and
empowering developers to build resilient products. We support our developers
during the application build phase in software run principals that includes
operational design, automation, capacity planning, monitoring that leads to fault-
tolerant, scalable products. We see the big picture and help create and enforce
operations standards while facilitating an agile and learning culture.
We support daily operations with a hyper focus on triage, root cause by
understanding the business impact of our products and subsequently performing
blameless post-mortems. The goal of every Business Operations team is to
engage early in the development lifecycle to be more proactive and upfront in
the development process, and to proactively manage production and change
activities to maximize customer experience and increase the overall value of
supported applications. Business Operations teams also focus on risk
management by tying all our activities together with an overarching
responsibility for compliance and risk mitigation across all our environments.
Ultimately, the role of Business Operations is to align Product and Customer
Focused priorities with Operational needs by providing continuous feedback
throughout the lifecycle.

Site Reliability Engineering:
o Serve as the primary contact responsible for ensuring application
scalability, performance, and resilience.
O Practice sustainable incident response and blameless post-mortems
while taking a holistic approach to problem solving and optimizing
time to recover.
O Automate data-driven alerts to proactively escalate issues. Work
with development teams to establish SLOs and improve reliability.

Role Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have experience in many of these areas:
• BS degree in Computer Science or related technical field involving coding
(e.g., physics or mathematics), or equivalent practical experience.
• Coding or scripting exposure.
• Appetite for change and pushing the boundaries of what can be done with
automation. Be curious about new technology, infrastructure, and
practices to scale our architecture and prepare for future growth.
• Experience with algorithms, data structures, scripting, pipeline
management, and software design
• Systematic problem-solving approach, coupled with strong communication
skills and a sense of ownership and drive.
• Interest in designing, analysing, and troubleshooting large-scale
distributed systems.
• Willingness and ability to learn and take on challenging opportunities and
to work as a member of matrix based diverse and geographically
distributed project team.
• Ability to balance doing things right with fixing things quickly. Flexible and
pragmatic, while working towards improving the long-term health of the
system.

expected system behaviour is understood and monitoring exists to detect
anomalies.

Manager Technology Risk Management

Overview

Manager, Technology Risk Management

Manage and support the 1st line Technology Risk Management function at MTS.

LOCATION: Pune (hybrid)

Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.

Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Mastercard Transaction Services (MTS) is the regulated legal entity within Mastercard that enables transaction services and related payment capabilities in line with applicable regulatory requirements. MTS retains regulatory accountability for its services, while Mastercard corporate functions and affiliated service providers deliver operational, technology and information security services under an oversight and assurance model. This structure requires strong governance, effective risk management, clear control ownership and ongoing evidence of regulatory compliance.

Role

This role supports the first line Technology Risk Management function for MTS, helping to operationalize the technology risk framework, coordinate regulatory and supervisory reporting, and provide assurance over technology, cyber and third-party risk obligations.

The role works closely with MTS leadership, Mastercard corporate functions, Information Security, Technology, Compliance, Operational Resilience, Legal Entity Management and Internal Audit.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, outcomes-focused technology risk professional who can operate effectively in a regulated environment, build trusted relationships across functions, and translate complex technology and cyber risk matters into clear, actionable insights for management and governance forums.

What are we looking for

-Experience in technology risk management, information security, cyber risk, IT audit, operational resilience, regulatory compliance or a related field.
-Strong understanding of technology and cyber risk frameworks, controls, risk assessment methodologies and issue remediation processes.
-Experience supporting regulated financial services, payments, technology or operational resilience environments is preferred.
-Experience managing or participating in the RCSA process, ideally within a financial services, IT or payments context, including experience working in first- or second-line risk teams or within third-line Internal Audit functions in a financial services environment.
-Familiarity with regulatory requirements such as DORA,EBA ICT Guidelines, operational and security risk reporting, ICT risk management, third-party risk management and control effectiveness reporting.
-Ability to coordinate across multiple stakeholders, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs under regulatory or governance timelines.
-Strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare concise reporting for senior management, committees, auditors and regulators.

Qualifications
-A bachelor's degree in technology, information security, computer science, risk management or a related discipline is preferred. Relevant professional experience will also be considered.
-Professional certifications such as CRISC, CISSP, CISM, CISA are desirable.
